resources.name: Adult Protective Services
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: Each California county has Adult Protective Services to help adults 60 and older, and disabled adults 18-59, who are being abused, neglected, or exploited or can't meet their own needs. Services are free.

eligibility.notes: For elders 60 or older, or dependent adults 18-59 with disabilities, who are believed to be victims of abuse, neglect or exploitation. No income limit and no cost. Call and enter your ZIP code to reach your county APS, 24/7.

resources.name: Aging and Disability Resource Connection - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Aging and Disability Resource Connections help people find and use long-term services at home. They offer referrals, one-on-one counseling, short-term help getting services, and help moving home from a hospital or nursing facility.

eligibility.notes: Open to anyone regardless of age, income, or disability. Services are through your local Area Agency on Aging.

resources.name: Bankruptcy resources
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: bankruptcy resources List of informational resources in bankruptcy FTC's Consumer debt advice Information from the Federal Trade Commission about debt relief services, credit counseling, debt consolidation, and bankruptcy. Get information on how to get out of debt.

resources.name: Behind on your energy bills? LIHEAP may be able to help.
resources.organization: California energy bills, weatherization and community assistance
resources.description: LIHEAP helps low-income households pay heating and cooling bills with a one-time payment. It may also offer weatherization to make homes safer and more energy efficient. Apply through your local LIHEAP agency.

eligibility.notes: Based on income, household size, where you live, and other factors. 2026 monthly income limits: $3,331.66 for 1 person, $4,356.83 for 2, $5,382.00 for 3, $6,407.16 for 4. Funding is limited and very vulnerable households get priority.

resources.name: Bringing Families Home Program
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: Bringing Families Home Program The Bringing Families Home (BFH) Program was established in 2016 to reduce the number of families in the child welfare system experiencing, or at risk of homelessness, to increase family reunification and to prevent foster care placement. BFH offers financial assistance and housing-related wraparound supportive services, including but not limited to: rental assistance, housing navigation, case management, security deposits, utility payments, moving costs, interim shelter assistance, legal services, and credit repair. As of Fiscal Year (FY) 2022-23, there are 53 counties and 25 Tribes and tribal entities operating a BFH program, with each program tailored to meet the needs of the local community. More information about participating BFH grantees is available in CFL 22/23-43. Eligibility BFH targets families involved with the child welfare system who are expe

eligibility.notes: Family must be involved with the child welfare system. Administered by each county; contact your county child welfare agency.

resources.name: CalFresh
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: CalFresh (SNAP) gives monthly food benefits to people and families with low income. How much you get depends on household size, income, and costs like rent and utilities.

resources.name: CalFresh Outreach
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: CalFresh gives monthly food benefits to low-income seniors age 60 and older, including those on SSI/SSP who could not get CalFresh before 2019. Contact your local Area Agency on Aging to see if you qualify.

eligibility.notes: California seniors at least 60 years old with low income, whether or not they get SSI or SSP. No specific income figure stated on the page.

resources.name: California Earned Income Tax Credit
resources.organization: California Franchise Tax Board
resources.description: CalEITC is a state tax credit for working people with low income. It can give you cash back or lower the tax you owe. For tax year 2025, earned income must be $32,900 or less. You claim it by filing a California tax return.

eligibility.notes: Must be at least 18 or have a qualifying child; earned income between $1 and $32,900 (tax year 2025); valid SSN or ITIN for everyone claimed; lived in California more than half the year; can't be claimed as a qualifying child of another taxpayer. Married filing separately has extra rules.

required_documents: California state tax return
Form FTB 3514 (include with your return)
Valid SSN or ITIN for you, your spouse/RDP, and any qualifying children

resources.name: California Training Benefits
resources.organization: California jobs, unemployment and disability benefits
resources.description: California Training Benefits let you go to school or job training while you keep getting unemployment benefits. You don't have to look for work while in training. EDD does not pay for tuition, books, or other costs.

eligibility.notes: Must have a current, valid unemployment claim and be in an eligible training program. Contact EDD before the 16th week of benefit payments to qualify for a training extension.

resources.name: CalWORKs Homeless Assistance
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: CalWORKs Homeless Assistance The CalWORKs Homeless Assistance (HA) Program was established to help families in the CalWORKs program meet the costs of securing or maintaining permanent housing or to provide emergency shelter when a family is experiencing homelessness. CalWORKs HA program serves eligible CalWORKs recipients or apparently eligible CalWORKs applicants, who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. CalWORKs HA can provide payments for temporary shelter for up to 16 days, once every 12 months with exceptions, as well as payments to secure or maintain housing, including a security deposit and last month’s rent, or up to two months of rent arrearages. For more information about the program, see the Homeless Assistance (HA) Fact Sheet. Types of Homeless Assistance Temporary HA, which helps families pay the costs of temporary shelter. 16 days of temporary shelter with exceptions, i

eligibility.notes: For CalWORKs recipients or apparently eligible applicants. Temporary shelter payments for up to 16 days once every 12 months, plus help with a security deposit or last month's rent.

resources.name: CalWORKs Housing Support Program
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: CalWORKs Housing Support Program The CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP) was established in 2014 to foster housing stability for families experiencing, or at risk of, homelessness in the CalWORKs program. HSP offers housing-related financial assistance – such as rental assistance, security deposits, utility payments, moving costs, and hotel/motel vouchers – alongside wraparound supportive services, which may include housing navigation, case management, referrals for legal services, and credit repair. As of Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25, fifty-six (56) counties operate HSP and each program is tailored to meet the needs of the local community. More information about participating HSP grantees is available in County Fiscal Letter (CFL) 24/25-11. Eligibility/For Whom HSP assists families in the CalWORKs program that are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of homelessness, including famili

eligibility.notes: Must be a family receiving CalWORKs. Apply through your county welfare office; counties prioritize families who are currently homeless.

resources.name: CFAP
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: CFAP gives state-funded food benefits to some noncitizens who can't get CalFresh only because of their immigration status. You use the same application as CalFresh, and the county decides which program you qualify for.

eligibility.notes: Noncitizens who are ineligible for CalFresh solely because of immigration status, such as green card holders who haven't met the 5-year or 40-work-quarter rule, parolees, conditional entrants, and people who are battered or abused. No age or income figures stated.

resources.name: CFAP Expansion
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: The CFAP expansion will give food benefits to Californians 55 and older who have low income, no matter their immigration status. It is not available yet; the page says it starts October 1, 2027.

eligibility.notes: Will cover income-eligible Californians age 55 or older who are excluded from CalFresh only because of immigration status. A Social Security number is not required if you don't have one. Starts October 1, 2027.

resources.name: Children and Family Services
resources.organization: San Mateo County Human Services Agency
resources.description: San Mateo County Children and Family Services protects children from abuse and neglect and helps families stay healthy and stable. It also handles child protective services, foster care, and adoptions. Call the Child Abuse Hotline to report concerns.

resources.name: Community-Based Adult Services - Medicare Services
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: CBAS is a day health program for adults with chronic medical, memory, or behavioral health conditions or disabilities who are on Medi-Cal. It offers nursing, therapy, meals, personal care, and rides to and from home.

eligibility.notes: Age 18 or older, currently eligible for Medi-Cal, and meet specific medical necessity rules.

resources.name: Connectivity Resources
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Connectivity Resources Older Adults benefit from two types of connectivity for home and community-based services: Broadband via Wi-Fi: Internet connection provided through router at a physical location such as a home, community center or place of business. Broadband via 5G: Internet connection provided through a cell tower by a specific cellular provider that generally allows for better mobility in a community as long the cellular provider services the associated area. Resources Free or low-cost resources. Some resources may limit or have special conditions for those who qualify (ex: only for low-income, limited by geographic area, requires a subscription, etc.) CDA Digital Connections Program, Home and community-based programs to help bridge the digital divide for older adults including purchasing digital devices, service plans, and training. Contact your local AAA, CBAS, MSSP, or PACE

eligibility.notes: Income limits apply; the amounts are not published on the page.

resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services

Some offer help with conservatorships. If they don't they may know local programs that do. Find out from your local court what type of services they offer. LawHelpCA Offers a lookup tool to help find legal aid offices, lawyer referral services, and other free and low-cost services in your county. County Law Library Law librarians offer legal resources for people who don't have a lawyer. Many libraries offer free self-help programs. You can also ask a law library a question in Live Chat. Lawyer Referral Service Directory of lawyer referral services throughout California Government services Department of Developmental Services Oversees the coordination and deliver of services to California living with d

eligibility.notes: Must be an Adult Protective Services client or in APS intake.

resources.name: County of San Mateo Veteran Service Providers Contacts
resources.organization: San Mateo County Human Services Agency
resources.description: Veteran Service Provider Data Base County Veteran Service Providers Address Book 07.28.2026 .pdf Join the Network Are you an organization or service provider that supports veterans and their families? Join our network database and be notified of community events and become more visible to our community veterans. Fill out the form and email is to: aayag@smcgov.org CVSO Community Network Form

resources.name: Court-based self-help services
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: Every California superior court has free self-help for people without a lawyer, mainly for family law and small claims. Staff can explain your case and help with forms, but they are not your lawyer and can't give legal advice.

eligibility.notes: Open to anyone who does not have their own lawyer; no income limit. Services are free. What you tell staff is not confidential.

resources.name: Digital Inclusion
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: California Department of Aging programs help older adults and people with disabilities get digital devices, internet service plans, and training. Call and say your county name to reach local help.

eligibility.notes: For older adults and people with disabilities, through county programs. No age or income figures stated.

resources.name: Dignity At Home Fall Prevention Program - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Dignity At Home helps adults 60+ and people with disabilities avoid falls. It offers in-home safety checks, home changes, safety equipment, and fall prevention training. Contact your local Area Agency on Aging.

eligibility.notes: Age 60 or older or have a disability; has fallen or is at risk of falling or of needing institutional care; adjusted household income no more than 80% of area median income.

resources.name: Disability Insurance Benefits
resources.organization: California jobs, unemployment and disability benefits
resources.description: Short-term payments for California workers who can't work and lose wages because of a non-work illness, injury, pregnancy, or surgery. Pays about $50 to $1,765 a week for up to 52 weeks.

eligibility.notes: You can't do your regular work for at least 8 days, lost wages because of the disability, were working or looking for work when it started, earned at least $300 with SDI taken out of your pay in your base period, and have a doctor/practitioner certify the disability. Part-time workers may qualify.

resources.name: Division: Behavioral Health and Recovery Services - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: San Mateo County's mental health and substance use services, including prevention, outpatient and inpatient treatment, residential care, detox, and medication-assisted treatment.

resources.name: DMV for Veterans
resources.organization: San Mateo County Human Services Agency
resources.description: Helps veterans get a Veteran designation on their California driver's license, veteran logo license plates, or Disabled Veteran plates through the County Veteran Service Office.

eligibility.notes: Veteran designation requires a discharge rating of at least General Discharge. Disabled Veteran plates require a VA-certified condition such as 100% service-connected disability or a service-connected disability affecting mobility, vision, or use of limbs.

required_documents: Military discharge papers (DD-214)
VA Award Letter (for Disabled Veteran plates, if first visit to the CVSO)
Proof of vehicle registration (for Disabled Veteran plates)

resources.name: Education Programs — Sacred Heart Community Service
resources.organization: Sacred Heart Community Service assistance programs
resources.description: Sacred Heart offers early learning and parenting support for families with babies and toddlers, plus after school and summer programs for low-income students in San José and Gilroy.

resources.name: Employment Services for People with Disabilities
resources.organization: California jobs, unemployment and disability benefits
resources.description: EDD helps people with disabilities find jobs with job listings, career coaching, workshops, skills testing, and links to community support through America's Job Centers.

resources.name: Energy Service — Sacred Heart Community Service
resources.organization: Sacred Heart Community Service assistance programs
resources.description: Helps low-income Santa Clara County households pay home energy bills with one HEAP payment a year ($328 to $521), and helps with PG&E's CARE discount.

eligibility.notes: Must live in Santa Clara County and have monthly household gross income below the page's income chart. Energy must come from PG&E, Silicon Valley Power, City of Palo Alto, be submetered, or included in rent. Non-emergency; payment can take 6-8 weeks.

required_documents: US government-issued photo ID of the applicant
All pages of your current month's energy bill
Proof of income from all sources for everyone in the household 18 or older

resources.name: Family Caregiver Services - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Gives family caregivers a break (respite care) and training. Services are provided through your local Area Agency on Aging.

eligibility.notes: Caregivers 18+ caring for someone 60+ or someone of any age with Alzheimer's or a related disorder; relatives (not parents) 55+ raising children under 18; relatives (including parents) 55+ caring for someone of any age with a disability.

resources.name: Finding a Job — Sacred Heart Community Service
resources.organization: Sacred Heart Community Service assistance programs
resources.description: Sacred Heart in San José helps job seekers with resumes, interview practice, job searching, and financial coaching. A new-member orientation is required.

resources.name: Food Assistance
resources.organization: San Mateo County Human Services Agency
resources.description: CalFresh gives people with low income a monthly amount on a debit-like card to help buy food. San Mateo County takes applications.

resources.name: Food Services - Samaritan House
resources.organization: Samaritan House food, housing, health and financial assistance
resources.description: Samaritan House offers a food pantry, weeknight take-out dinners, weekend lunch, after-school snacks, and meal delivery for seniors and people with disabilities. A food voucher needs an application.

resources.name: From Service to Success
resources.organization: California jobs, unemployment and disability benefits
resources.description: EDD gives veterans, service members, and their spouses priority for job referrals and training, plus help from veteran job specialists at America's Job Centers.

resources.name: Get free or low-cost legal help
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: Every California superior court has a free self-help center that helps people without a lawyer understand their case and forms. The page also points to legal aid and lawyer referral services.

eligibility.notes: Open to anyone; no income or residency requirement stated for court self-help centers. Separate legal aid programs depend on income and type of problem.

We can help with: Food and groceries Emergency housing and shelter Utility bill assistance Referrals to additional services Video en español Start here: Contact a Core Service Agency If you are experiencing homelessness or are at risk of losing housing, your local agency can help. resources.name: Health & Dental - Samaritan House
resources.organization: Samaritan House food, housing, health and financial assistance
resources.description: Clinics in San Mateo and Redwood City offering medical, dental, vision, and mental health care for low-income, uninsured San Mateo County residents. Start with a case manager referral.

eligibility.notes: For low-income, uninsured people living in San Mateo County, often those who earn too much for Medi-Cal and have no job-based insurance. Needs a referral from a Samaritan House case manager; appointment only.

resources.name: Health Care Services - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: The county Health Coverage Unit helps people sign up for health coverage like Medi-Cal, Covered California, and county programs such as ACE. Help and screening are free. Call to start.

eligibility.notes: Free help for San Mateo County residents. Which program you qualify for depends on income (FPL-based limits), immigration status, where you live, and age, disability, family size or medical need. Legal status is not required for County-funded coverage.

required_documents: Proof of income for all working household members (if any)
Proof of identity
Proof of address
Social Security or Tax ID number (if you have one)
Immigration or work documents (if you have them)

resources.name: Home & Community Services - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Helps adults 60 and older stay independent with in-home help, adult day care, respite, transportation, legal help, and care management through local Area Agencies on Aging.

eligibility.notes: People 60 or older, regardless of income.

resources.name: Home Safe Program
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: Home Safe Program The Home Safe Program was established in 2018 to prevent or address homelessness to support the safety and housing stability of individuals involved in Adult Protective Services (APS), individuals in the APS intake process, or who may be served by a Tribal social services agency and who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Home Safe offers a range of strategies to address and prevent homelessness and support ongoing housing stability for APS clients, including housing-related intensive case management, housing-related financial assistance, deep cleaning to maintain safe housing, eviction prevention, landlord mediation, and more. Fifty-eight (58) counties operate a Home Safe program, and each program is tailored to meet the needs of the local community. Twenty-three tribal grantees operate a Home Safe program. For more information about county funding, refer to C

eligibility.notes: Must be an Adult Protective Services client or in APS intake (older adults or dependent adults experiencing abuse, neglect, or financial exploitation). Administered by each county APS office.

resources.name: Housing & Shelter - Samaritan House
resources.organization: Samaritan House food, housing, health and financial assistance
resources.description: OUR SERVICES Housing & Shelter Housing assistance, emergency rent / utility assistance and eviction avoidance Homelessness Prevention Samaritan House helps families avoid homelessness with emergency rent and assistance with utility bills. Rental assistance continues to be one of the most important and common needs of our clients as it allows families to avoid eviction and remain in their homes. This is one of the least costly and most effective services we provide to meet the housing need of our clients. Housing Placement and Stabilization Case managers work with clients to explore what contributed to their housing instability and address those issues. They provide support with housing applications, qualification for housing programs, and work closely with landlords to create more housing opportunities for our clients. Coordinated Entry System (CES) Samaritan House administers San Mateo

eligibility.notes: San Mateo County residents. Emergency rent and utility help, eviction avoidance, and three shelters (Safe Harbor in South San Francisco, Pacific Emergency in Redwood City, El Camino House in San Mateo). Call (650) 347-3648 or apply online at apply.samaritanhousesanmateo.org.

resources.name: Housing and Disability Advocacy Program
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: For people experiencing homelessness who likely qualify for disability benefits. Offers help applying for benefits, case management, and housing help like rent, deposits, and shelter. Run by counties.

eligibility.notes: For people experiencing homelessness who are likely eligible for disability benefits; chronic homelessness is prioritized. Run by your county; contact your county point of contact.

resources.name: Housing Assistance — Sacred Heart Community Service
resources.organization: Sacred Heart Community Service assistance programs

We assist with: Past-due rent Emergency security deposit Mortgage Other financial assistance tied to housing stability One must be a resident of Santa Clara County for at least thirty days before applying. All financial assistance goes directly to the landlord, not to the member applying. SHCS serves the following zip codes for Housing Assistance: 95008, 95110, 95111, 95112 (South of Santa Clara Street), 95113, 95116, 95117, 95118, 95120, 95123, 95124, 95125, 95126, 95128, 95136 note: Assistance from the HPS program is NOT restricted to these zip codes If you do not see your zip code listed, CLICK HERE to find the agency that serves your zip c

eligibility.notes: Low-income Santa Clara County residents who have lived in the county at least 30 days. Covers past-due rent, emergency security deposits, and mortgage help. Payment goes directly to the landlord. Limited to the ZIP codes listed on the page.

resources.name: Immigration resources: Legal help
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: Immigration resources: Legal help PRINT EMAIL TEXT Hire a lawyer or get free legal help Before you start Immigration law is very complex. You can hire a licensed lawyer or accredited representative to help with an immigration case. Use these sites to find out if a lawyer is licensed in the state of California or if an immigration representative is accredited: State Bar attorney search Find an immigration lawyer The resource listed below, provided by the California State Bar, can help you find an immigration lawyer. You can also look for others online or ask organizations you trust in your area for help. resources.name: Individuals & Families : CA Department of Developmental Services
resources.organization: California developmental disability and family support
resources.description: The state Department of Developmental Services supports people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, such as autism, cerebral palsy, and epilepsy, through local regional centers.

resources.name: Legal Services - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Legal help for older adults on housing, fraud, elder abuse, Social Security, SSI, Medicare, Medi-Cal, and more, through your local Area Agency on Aging.

eligibility.notes: People 60 or older, regardless of income. The page also mentions adults with disabilities.

resources.name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
resources.organization: California energy bills, weatherization and community assistance
resources.description: Helps low-income households pay heating and cooling bills, get crisis help with energy, and get free weatherization upgrades. Apply through your local energy agency.

resources.name: Meal Programs - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: Healthy meals for older adults, served at community sites or delivered to homes, plus nutrition education. Offered through local Area Agencies on Aging.

eligibility.notes: Group meals: age 60+, their spouse (any age), or a person with a disability living where meals are served. Home-delivered: age 60+ with limited ability to leave home or cook, their spouse, or a person with a disability living with a participant.

resources.name: Medicare Counseling (HICAP) - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: HICAP gives free, private one-on-one help with Medicare, long-term care insurance, and other health insurance questions, including appeals. It is for people on Medicare or about to get it.

eligibility.notes: Counseling is for people 65 or older who are eligible for Medicare, people under 65 with a disability who are eligible for Medicare, and people who will soon be eligible for Medicare. Education events are open to any age.

resources.name: Mental Health Services - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: County Behavioral Health & Recovery Services offers mental health care at clinics across the county for all ages. Walk in for a same-day screening, or call the Access Call Center for help finding care.

eligibility.notes: All ages. Request services by calling the Access Call Center or walking in to any regional clinic for Same Day Assistance (first-come, first-served). Contact page: BHRS serves people who are uninsured or have Medi-Cal, CareAdvantage, Medicare, ACE or HealthWorx.

resources.name: Multipurpose Senior Services Program - Medicare Services
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: MSSP helps adults 60 and older on Medi-Cal who need nursing-home-level care stay at home. A care team makes a plan and can arrange services like care management, adult day care, home repair, respite, rides, and meals.

eligibility.notes: Must be 60 or older, eligible for Medi-Cal under a qualifying primary Medi-Cal aid code, and certified or certifiable for placement in a skilled nursing facility.

resources.name: Project Roomkey
resources.organization: California Department of Social Services benefits
resources.description: Project Roomkey/Housing and Homelessness COVID Response Project Roomkey was established in March 2020 as part of the state response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The purpose of Project Roomkey and Rehousing Strategy was to provide non-congregate shelter options, such as hotels and motels, for people experiencing homelessness, to protect human life, and to minimize strain on health care system capacity. As the response to the pandemic evolved, so did Project Roomkey. In November 2020, a new phase of Project Roomkey began, called Project Roomkey and Rehousing Strategy. This new phase of the program built on existing emergency shelter efforts while also supporting permanent transitions to safe and stable housing to ensure homelessness is non-recurring. Project Roomkey and Rehousing Strategy gives people who are experiencing homelessness and recovering from COVID-19, or have been exposed to COVI

eligibility.notes: COVID-era hotel shelter program that is winding down; site closures vary by county. Not a program people can apply to directly.

resources.name: Protecting Older and Dependent Adults
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: Adult Protective Services helps older adults (60+) and dependent adults (18-59) who are being abused, neglected, or taken advantage of. Call the 24/7 line to report abuse. You can stay anonymous.

eligibility.notes: For adults 60 and older and dependent adults ages 18-59 who are victims of abuse, neglect or exploitation. Anyone can report; non-mandated reporters may report without giving their name. Home Safe program: must be an APS client (or in intake), experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness, and agree to participate.

resources.description: A California Courts list of free child support help. It covers your court's family law facilitator or self-help center, a support calculator, legal aid lookup, and how to apply at your county child support agency.

resources.name: Resources for debt lawsuits
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: A California Courts list of free help if you are sued over a debt. It covers court self-help centers, legal aid lookup, law libraries, lawyer referrals, and consumer protection offices that explain your rights with debt collectors.

resources.name: Resources for small claims cases
resources.organization: California Courts free legal help and self-help services
resources.description: A California Courts list of free help with small claims cases. It covers small claims advisors, court self-help centers, legal aid lookup, law libraries, and state consumer offices where you can file complaints.

resources.name: Senior Employment Training - Consumer
resources.organization: California older adult, caregiver and disability services
resources.description: SCSEP is a paid job training program for low-income, unemployed adults 55 and older. People work about 20 hours a week at nonprofits or government agencies, earn minimum wage, and build skills for a regular job.

eligibility.notes: Must be 55 or older and unemployed. Priority goes to veterans and qualified spouses, people over 65, people with disabilities, people with limited English, rural residents, people who are homeless or at risk, and formerly incarcerated people. Not every local agency offers it.

resources.name: Services: Aging and Disability - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: Aging & Disability Services helps older adults and people with disabilities. It offers abuse protection, in-home care (IHSS), public guardian help, and referrals to local services. A 24-hour line is available.

resources.name: Services: General Health - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: San Mateo Medical Center is the county's public hospital and clinic system. It offers primary care, dental care, specialty care, women's health, and emergency care for people across the county.

resources.name: Services: Mental Health & Substance Use - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: County Behavioral Health & Recovery Services offers mental health and substance use care, including treatment, detox, and recovery support. Call the 24/7 Access Call Center to get connected.

eligibility.notes: Serves people of all cultures and ages needing mental health and/or substance use support. Access Call Center is the entry point for Medi-Cal members seeking non-emergency care. Serves people who are uninsured or have Medi-Cal, CareAdvantage, Medicare, ACE or HealthWorx.

resources.name: Services: Pregnancy, Children, & Families - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: Family Health Services helps low-income parents and children in San Mateo County. Services include home visits, health screenings, vaccine clinics, lead checks, WIC nutrition help, and support for kids with special health needs.

eligibility.notes: Focuses on San Mateo County parents and children who are low-income and have faced health inequities.

resources.name: Services: Where to Get Care - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: San Mateo Medical Center is the county's public hospital and clinics. It offers primary and specialty care for the whole family, plus emergency, surgery, and rehab services. New patients can call for help getting started.

resources.name: Services: Women, Infants & Children (WIC) Program - San Mateo County Health
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: WIC gives healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding help, and health referrals to low-income pregnant or new moms and children under 5. Dads, grandparents, and foster parents can apply for kids too.

eligibility.notes: Serves pregnant women, breastfeeding women up to 1 year postpartum, non-breastfeeding women up to 6 months postpartum, women with a pregnancy loss in the past 6 months, and infants/children under 5 (including foster children). Must meet income guidelines (see CDPH); families on Medi-Cal, CalFresh or CalWORKs qualify.

resources.name: Support for Older and Dependent Adults
resources.organization: San Mateo County Health
resources.description: In-Home Supportive Services (IHSS) pays for help at home, like cooking, cleaning, bathing, and rides to the doctor. It is for people on Medi-Cal who are 65+, blind, or disabled, so they can stay safely at home.

eligibility.notes: Must be 65 or older, blind, or disabled (disability lasting 1 year or longer; disabled children may qualify), live in San Mateo County in your own home, be enrolled in active full-scope Medi-Cal, and complete an in-home assessment. Services may be free or you may pay part based on income.

required_documents: Online referral form
IHSS Health Care Certification Form (SOC 873), completed by a licensed health care professional within 45 days of applying

resources.name: Supported Employment Program - CA Department of Rehabilitation
resources.organization: California rehabilitation, independent living and assistive technology
resources.description: The Department of Rehabilitation's Supported Employment Program gives people with the most significant disabilities a job coach to help them learn a job, do it well, and keep working. DOR services usually last up to 24 months.

eligibility.notes: For people with a most significant disability, including youth. You apply through the Department of Rehabilitation's general application for DOR services.

resources.name: Unemployment Benefits
resources.organization: California jobs, unemployment and disability benefits
resources.description: Unemployment benefits give short-term weekly payments of $40 to $450 to California workers who lost their job or had their hours cut through no fault of their own. The amount depends on what you earned in the past 18 months.

eligibility.notes: Must have a Social Security number and, if not a U.S. citizen, work authorization. Must have earned enough wages in the base period (past 18 months). Must be fully or partly unemployed through no fault of your own, and able, available, ready, and looking for work each week. People who quit or were fired may still qualify.

required_documents: Social Security number
Photo ID (such as a driver's license, ID card, or passport)
A second identity document (such as a W2, utility bill, or birth certificate)
Employer names, addresses, dates worked, gross wages, and hours for the past 18 months
Most recent employer and supervisor contact information, last day worked, and last week's gross wages
USCIS document (such as a Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card), if not a U.S. citizen
Standard Form 8, if you worked for the federal government in the last 18 months
DD214 Member Copy 4, if you served in the military in the last 18 months

resources.name: Utility Assistance — Sacred Heart Community Service
resources.organization: Sacred Heart Community Service assistance programs
resources.description: Sacred Heart helps low-income Santa Clara County households with utility bills. HEAP gives a once-a-year credit on your energy bill. WRAP pays up to $1,000 a year on your water bill. Because funding is limited, HEAP help is not guaranteed.

eligibility.notes: For Santa Clara County residents who meet the program's income limits. The posted monthly limit is $3,331 for a 1-person household and $4,356 for 2 (up to $8,841 for 8). HEAP covers PG&E, Silicon Valley Power, City of Palo Alto, submetered, and included-in-rent energy. WRAP requires that you pay a residential water bill due within 30 to 60 days. A HEAP priority plan is in effect, so some income-eligible households may be denied.

required_documents: Current proof of income for everyone in the household, or proof of CalFresh or CalWORKs from the last 30 days (for WRAP)
Completed application
Residential water bill (for WRAP)
